newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea asks North to resume Red Cross talks.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea asks North to resume Red Cross talks.

text.p: The South Korean Red Cross on Friday asked its North Korean counterpart to resume talks next week on speeding delivery of Southern food aid, a statement said.

The proposal, made over a telephone hotline at the border, made clear the South would inform the North Korean Red Cross of the size of aid -- the issue that led to a deadlock in previous contacts this month.
Kang Young-hoon, president of the South Korean Red Cross, proposed a meeting either in Seoul, Pyongyang or at the border village of Panmunjom on May 23.

Inter-Korean Red Cross talks were held for the first time in nearly five years on May 3 and 5 in Beijing at Pyongyang's insistence. But they stalled after the North demanded to know the exact amount of aid.
The South wants to set up channels for direct relief deliveries rather than using the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies as a go-between.
The Southern Red Cross is due to deliver 3,600 tonnes of Chinese corn by train next week from China, the first batch of 15,000 tonnes donated by Southern civic groups to help stave off famine.
